revised: 2026-09-25: fork point moved from core-u00058 (150M, pooled 1525) to f100M (pooled 1558) per coordinator
2026-09-25: F1 = GNS recipe (analysis/gradient-noise-scale ff852474); F1b dropped; F2 folded onto F1 at equal per-update compute

fork_point.why: statistically tied with f50M (1559) and the strongest arm A snapshot; 150M sits about 2 sigma below the peak; f100M is also the parent of showiness candidate 2, so both share a baseline
fork_point.optimizer_state: none (61.7 MB weights-only snapshot; core-u00058.pt with optimizer is 185 MB). Every arm, including the control, starts with a fresh AdamW at the same settings.
fork_point.retention_baseline: each arm measures its per-pace anchor KL baseline at f100M on start, identically

arms.control: unchanged arm A recipe (ppo-v1 config: 544 games, minibatch 128, 2 epochs, lr 3e-6, clip-norm 0.7) from f100M, fresh Adam
arms.F1_gns_recipe: optimizer changes only at 544 games/update: minibatch 2048; lr 1.2e-5 (sqrt(B) scaling) with KL targeting at 0.003-0.005 and the hard max_update_kl cap kept; gradient clip-norm about 4 (2-3x median pre-clip norm); 1 epoch. Compared against control.
arms.F2_allocation_on_F1: F1 plus strength-weighted allocation at equal per-update compute (games/update sloth 16, relaxed 16, normal 20, fast 28, top_humans 37, super_human 56, frame_perfect 57 = about 3.0M frames/update, same as the current 2.98M) plus pace weights (FP 3, SH 3, TH 2, Fast 1.5, Normal 1, Relaxed 0.5, Sloth 0.5) in balance_pace_credit. Compared against F1.
arms.F3_retention_hinge: control recipe; retention penalises only anchor KL above each pace's fork-point baseline; coefficient and hard limit unchanged. Compared against control.

budget: equal frames per arm, about 50M (100M -> 150M), snapshots every 12.5M
primary_metric: slope of the pooled strength-weighted L14-spawn rating (tools.rating_pool, anchor champion-retention-mixed-v2) versus frames, arm minus control, over the 5 snapshots including the shared f100M point
power_note: about +-12 Elo per snapshot; 50M-frame arms resolve slope differences of about 50 Elo per 100M or more
evidence: drmc-rl-diag-data: curve.json, replay.json, gradients-u58.json, gns/analysis-u58.json; GPU diagnostics (value fits, epochs, branch rollouts) pending in morning_queue.sh and may revise F1/F3; GNS: drmc-rl-gns-data/analysis.{json,txt} (policy B_noise about 3e5 decisions, flat across training; 4-10% of full-update gradient is signal)
F1b_decision: Not run. 4x games (about 2176/update, about 11.9M frames) fits only about 4 updates in 50M frames, so each 12.5M snapshot is a single update and the slope rests on about 4 noisy points. GNS's other point, extra games for the 32-game paces instead of sloth, agrees with the strength-weighted allocation, and F2 delivers it at equal compute by moving games from sloth/relaxed (sloth and relaxed currently use 24% of rollout compute; under the weights 2-3%). So F2 is folded onto F1 instead of into an F1b. Revisit a larger games-per-update arm with a 150M+ budget.

wall_time_estimates.basis: arm A ppo-v1: about 3,535 frames/s overall (rollout about 540 s + optimizer about 390 s per 2.98M-frame update; inference-bound). F1/F2 optimizer: 1 epoch at 2048 is estimated at about 200 s/update including checks. These are estimates, not benchmarks.
wall_time_estimates.sequential_all_four: about 14.6 h of GPU time, plus rating-pool evaluation on the distributed arena (not tf3090)
wall_time_estimates.in_pairs: (control, F1) then (F2, F3): about 5.5-6.5 h per pair, about 11-13 h total, assuming about 1.3-1.5x aggregate throughput. The binding limit is 4 CPU cores (planner_workers 3 each would oversubscribe; use 2 each), not RAM or GPU memory. The pairing is untested; measure the first pair's frames/s in the first update and fall back to sequential if aggregate < 1.2x.
wall_time_estimates.memory: keep MemAvailable >= 4 GB; the GPU (24 GB) fits two trainers at minibatch 2048 per the GNS bench

preconditions: Trainer source snapshot, native libraries (libdrmario_pool.so, libdrm_reach_full.so) and ppo.log live in ~/.cache/drmc-rl/afterstate-core on tf3090 (src-0f36d78d, native/). Point each fork's native_library and working directory there. Never use /dev/shm on tf3090 for scratch, checkouts or logs.
